scope_note: Disposition-only triage of the 21 directional unmatched-family entries identified by four-set-protocol-census.json (AP RX-only 8, Remote RX-only 1, Remote TX-only 9, AP TX-only 3). Does not reopen the proven core protocol (G/S/!/I/+/MC/LL/F0/E0/etc). Uses existing evidence first; a small number of tiny bounded static lookups (Ghidra disasm/xrefs, a raw firmware byte scan) were made only to decide executable/real-vs-literal status for the explicitly flagged priority cases (D, bare W, IX, B_UNKNOWN). No Unicorn, no SMT, no broad residual-function classification, no full semantic reversal of any family.

disposition_legend.REQUIRED_FOR_REPLACEMENT: The family's real, exercised behavior must be replicated by a replacement.
disposition_legend.REQUIRED_PARSER_COMPATIBILITY: A replacement must remain able to ACCEPT/parse this frame for compatibility, even though its own necessity/trigger is not fully understood.
disposition_legend.REQUIRED_TX_COMPATIBILITY: A replacement must remain able to SEND this frame for an existing peer to understand.
disposition_legend.LEGACY_OR_OTHER_PRODUCT: Evidence points to a different product, mode, or firmware generation, not this shipped configuration.
disposition_legend.DORMANT_OR_UNREACHED: Real, executable code exists but no producer/consumer was found in the examined firmware pair -- not asserted useless, only currently unreached.
disposition_legend.VARIANT_OR_FRAMING_MISMATCH: A real, precise mismatch between what one side sends and what the other side's dispatch structurally expects.
disposition_legend.WEAK_EVIDENCE_ONLY: Evidence tier too thin to support any stronger claim (e.g. a literal with no confirmed reference).
disposition_legend.UNRESOLVED_PRESERVE_AS_GAP: Genuinely open; deliberately not forced into a stronger disposition.

families.direction: unmatched (Remote TX only), precise variant/framing mismatch with AutoPilot RX
families.executable_status: Both sides definitely executable. Remote: real send (0x591c) of the literal 'W|' (no digit) in one branch. AutoPilot: mechanically re-examined this session (disasm 0x85c8-0x8650) -- the top-level 'W' check (0x85d8, cmp r3,#0x57) is reached for ANY message starting with 'W', then reads the SECOND byte and compares it to '0' (-> dedicated W0 handler, 0x72ac) and '1' (-> dedicated W1 handler, 0x8628-region). When the second byte is NEITHER '0' NOR '1' (which is exactly what a bare 'W|' frame supplies -- its second byte is the pipe terminator), execution falls through into a SHARED, GENERIC tail block (0x8628 onward: clears a flag, checks a 3-valued state, and either continues into more shared per-channel logic at 0x8648 or calls a separate shared poller routine at 0x541c) that is ALSO reached from other, unrelated contexts -- it is not W0's or W1's own logic, and not a hard error/drop either.
families.known_peer: Both sides exist and are both real; the mismatch is structural, not an absence of any code.
families.known_context: Bare 'W|' emitted from one specific Remote code branch ('zero branch' per existing notes); the AutoPilot's fallthrough tail is shared, generic per-channel/poller logic whose relationship to a 'W' context specifically was not chased further (matches this pass's bounded-lookup discipline).
families.replacement_relevance: PRECISE CHARACTERIZATION (as requested): this is a real protocol framing gap, not a parser bug and not silent data loss -- the AutoPilot's dispatch structurally expects a distinguishing 3rd byte after 'W' but does not hard-fail without one; a bare 'W|' is absorbed into unrelated shared tail code rather than either intended W0/W1 behavior. A replacement should NOT assume bare W is equivalent to either W0 or W1, and should decide deliberately (not accidentally, by falling through shared code) what a malformed/short W frame should do.
families.remaining_unknown: The real-world consequence of reaching the 0x8628/0x8648/0x541c shared tail from this specific entry point was not traced end-to-end (would require reopening the shared per-channel/poller logic in full, out of this pass's bounded scope).
